body:
incident-bot: ALERT: prod-serving-pool-pv1 queue length > 1000, 95th token latency 2.8s, error spike 5xx+10% (auto-created incident 1801234567)

alex: i'm on it — seeing steady increase starting ~02:12 UTC. p50 still ok but p95/p99 blown out. continuous batching backlog growing.

jess: fyi that's the pool serving low-cost hosts + free-tier. seems like a bad mix of long and short seq requests. suspect batching parameters are too conservative for the current QPS.

alex: can we trade some latency for throughput temporarily? blocking customers are getting 429s. want to avoid full route disable if possible.

jess: propose temporary changes: increase `max_batch_size`, bump `batch_window_ms`, enable continuous batching on pool `pv1` for non-SLA routes. quick command I plan to run from runtime admin:

```bash
# run from control plane (dry-run first)
runtimectl update-pool --pool pv1 --set continuous_batching=true --set batch_window_ms=75 --set max_batch_size=48 --dry-run
```

jess: dry-run looks good, kernel selection stays stable. downside: tail latency increases ~200-500ms for single-request traffic.

alex: okay do it but scope to `tier:free` routes only. also add a global soft QPS cap for anonymous keys to reduce noisy neighbors.

jess: executing live change now (scoped to `tier:free`).

ops-bot: ACTION: applying update to pool pv1 (scope: route.tag==tier:free). request id 6f3c4d.

ops-bot: UPDATE: change applied at 1801234612.

carla: putting a short-term route throttle in front of the public API to smooth bursts: `rate-limit: 10rps per key (burst 20)` for keys without SLA tag. pushing now.

support-bot: note: we routed critical-customer `acme-inc` to dedicated pool `pv-ded-3` earlier, they are unaffected.

mira: taking over on-call, will monitor for 30m and contact customers if regressions. alex — handoff to me.

alex: handing off, i'm available but switching to async. mira, see dashboards namespace `prod:batching:p95` and `prod:queue:len`.

mira: initial customer impact check: 3 low-touch customers reported timeouts (support tickets #554, #555, #556). escalated customers unaffected. notifying SRE channel to watch kernel error rates.

jess: metrics after change (t+90s): queue length down from 1100 -> 220, p95 token latency dropped from 2.8s -> 1.6s, overall throughput +42%. single-request p99 increased ~320ms for free-tier keys. error rate 5xx down to baseline.

mira: good tradeoff. can we make this automatic next time based on queue depth?
jess: we have proto for dynamic batching thresholds, but not enabled in prod. short-term: keeping manual config for the next 3 hours, then scale down.

carla: re: rate limits — traffic shaping reduced noise by ~30%. I'll keep the soft cap for 2 hours and ramp down if stable.

alex: do we need to notify any customers formally? support-bot, please tag the 3 low-touch customers with brief note: "We've applied temporary batching+routing changes to improve throughput; you may see slightly higher latency on single-request calls. No functional regressions expected."

support-bot: message queued to #support-incidents with ticket refs.

mira: logging mitigation steps for postmortem: 1) flag incident, 2) config changes (pool pv1 continuous_batching=true, batch_window_ms=75, max_batch_size=48), 3) route throttle keys without SLA to 10rps, 4) monitor.

jess: also capturing the exact runtimectl commands and the ops-bot request id. saving diffs to infra-config repo.

incident-bot: NOTE: escalation timer set for +30m.

mira: 30m update: metrics holding. queue stable 200-260, p95 ~1.5-1.7s, total 5xx back to normal. I'm going to leave changes in place for 2 hours then start a controlled rollback window (reduce batch_window_ms to 50 then to 25) while watching error budget.

alex: nice work. suggest follow-up action: add a `batching-emergency` policy that can be toggled per-pool and per-tier (with runbooks). avoids manual CLI run in future.

jess: +1 — will draft RFC and include metric thresholds for auto-toggle (queue_len>800 or p95>2s for 2m).

mira: closing incident stream in slack — we'll file postmortem template and assign owners. If anyone sees regressions ping me. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: incident 1801234567 resolved at 1801234789 (mitigation applied, monitoring stable).

mira: notes for postmortem: impact: free-tier increased latency ~0.3s median for single requests; benefit: eliminated 429s/5xx for majority of traffic; root-cause: mixed workload hitting same pool + conservative batching params. remediation: dynamic batching, per-tier pools, and improved noisy-neighbor detection.

jess: I'll add runtime metrics to the alert rule to include queue_len and batch_window usage so future alerts contain the batching state.

carla: leaving soft rate-limit in place for 1.5h more. will update when removed.

mira: thanks team. closing here.
